root_cause.text: The f2fs_sbi_show() function reads extension_count, hot_ext_count, and extension_list without holding sbi->sb_lock, allowing a concurrent sysfs write to modify these values and cause an inconsistent state (e.g., a count larger than the actual array size), leading to potential out-of-bounds access.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds f2fs_down_read(&sbi->sb_lock) before reading the counts and iterating over the extension_list, and f2fs_up_read(&sbi->sb_lock) after the formatting loop. The commit description explicitly states that the read path lacks protection and that concurrent modification can cause inconsistent count and array contents, leading to out-of-bounds access.

intent_record.intent_summary: Protect reading of extension_count and hot_ext_count under sb_lock to prevent race conditions when displaying extension list in sysfs.
intent_record.what: Moved initialization of cold_count and hot_count variables into a critical section by acquiring f2fs_down_read(&sbi->sb_lock) before reading extension_count and hot_ext_count from raw_super; variable declarations are separated from assignments.
intent_record.how: The change ensures that reading extension_count and hot_ext_count from the superblock is done under sb_lock, preventing concurrent modification races and ensuring consistent display of the extension list in sysfs.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix missing read lock release in f2fs_sbi_show when displaying hot file extensions.
intent_record.what: Added a call to f2fs_up_read(&sbi->sb_lock) before the return statement in f2fs_sbi_show, within the block that iterates over hot file extensions.
intent_record.how: This releases the read lock on sbi->sb_lock that was acquired earlier, preventing a lock leak and potential deadlock or incorrect lock accounting when the function returns from that code path.
